name: title
description: IN1900 Introduction to Programming for Scientific Applications

name: description
description: Python from the first variable to ODE solvers: loops, lists, functions, files, arrays, plotting, classes, and the numerical methods the course builds on them, decomposed into what the student has to be able to read, write and explain without aids.

name: slots.courseName
description: IN1900, introductory programming for scientific applications at the University of Oslo

name: slots.expressionFocus
description: mixes up = and ==; prints a value inside a function when the task asks for it to be returned; confuses an index with the element at that index; gets off-by-one errors at the ends of range and linspace; passes an expression where a function is expected; compares floats with == in a test; guesses the output of a piece of code instead of tracing it line by line; leaves out imports in written answers; and describes a numerical method without saying how the step size or the number of terms affects the error

name: slots.courseSpecifics
description: IN1900 is examined with no aids at all: a two-hour multiple-choice midterm that mostly tests reading and tracing code, and a four-hour final that mixes multiple choice with short programs the student writes without running them. Practise for that: have the student predict what code prints by tracing it before anything is run, and write short functions from memory. Use Python 3 with numpy and matplotlib. Give hints and small fragments of code, not complete solutions. Many students have little or no programming experience from before.

name: topicOrder
description: Python basics;Branching and loops;Lists and dictionaries;Functions;Testing and debugging;Files, input and exceptions;Arrays and plotting;Classes;Numerical methods;Difference equations;Differential equations

name: keywords
description: Python; programming; programmering; scientific programming; numpy; matplotlib; classes; object-oriented programming; ODE; Forward Euler; Runge-Kutta; ODESolver; difference equations; numerical differentiation; Taylor series; Newton's method; exam preparation; midterm; IN1900; UiO

name: Variable and assignment
description:
Variable: a name that refers to a value stored in memory.
Assignment: x = expression works out the right-hand side first and then lets the name on the left refer to the result. Assigning a new value to one name later does not change another name that got its value from it earlier.
instruction: Students read = as mathematical equality. Use x = x + 1, and y = x followed by x = 3, as the test cases.

name: Data types
description:
int: a whole number, such as 7 or -3.
float: a decimal number, such as 2.5 or 9.81; a calculation with at least one float gives a float.
str: text in quotes, such as 'hello'.
bool: True or False.
type(x): the built-in function that tells which type a value has.

name: Calculate with Python's operators
description: use +, -, *, /, //, % and ** with the right order of operations, and predict whether each result is an int or a float.
instruction: Include integer division and remainder (// and %), and that 2**3 is a power while 2^3 is not.

name: Floating-point number and round-off error
description:
Floating-point number: the computer's approximation of a real number with a limited number of digits.
Round-off error: the small difference between the stored number and the exact value, which is why 0.1 + 0.2 == 0.3 is False.

name: Print results with f-strings
description: print text and values with f-strings, choose the width and the number of decimals with format codes such as :8.3f, :g and :e, and line up a table in columns.

name: Module and import
description:
Module: a file of ready-made functions and constants, such as math or numpy, that a program loads with import.
Import: import math gives math.sin, from math import sin gives sin directly, and import numpy as np gives np.sin.

name: Use mathematical functions from a module
description: compute with sqrt, exp, log, sin, cos, pi and factorial from the math module, remembering that log is the natural logarithm and that angles are in radians.

name: Built-in functions to know by heart
description:
len(x): the number of elements in x
range(a, b, s): the integers from a up to but not including b, in steps of s
sum(x): the sum of the elements of x
max(x) and min(x): the largest and the smallest element of x
abs(x): the absolute value of x
int(x), float(x), str(x): x converted to that type
sorted(x): a new list with the elements of x in increasing order
zip(a, b): the pairs (a[0], b[0]), (a[1], b[1]), ... up to the shorter of the two
enumerate(a): the pairs (0, a[0]), (1, a[1]), ...
input(prompt): the line the user types, as a string

name: Work with strings
description: index and slice a string, join strings with + and join, split a line into words with split (also on a separator such as ';'), and test whether a substring occurs with in.

name: Boolean expression
description:
Boolean expression: an expression whose value is True or False, usually built from comparisons with ==, !=, <, <=, > and >=.
Logical operators: and, or and not; not is applied first, then and, then or, unless parentheses say otherwise.

name: Evaluate compound boolean expressions
description: work out by hand the value of an expression that combines comparisons, and, or, not, in and parentheses, including comparisons between list or array elements.

name: Branch with if, elif and else
description: write and trace an if-elif-else block, and explain that only the first branch whose test is true is run, while separate if-tests are each checked in turn.

name: For loop and range
description:
For loop: repeats a block once for every element of a sequence, with the loop variable taking each value in turn.
range(start, stop, step): the integers from start up to, but not including, stop.

name: While loop
description: While loop: repeats a block for as long as a condition is true. The condition is checked before every pass, so the block has to change something the condition depends on.

name: Trace a loop by hand
description: follow a for or while loop pass by pass in a table of the variables' values, and state the values when the loop ends, getting the first and the last pass right.
instruction: This is the core skill of the midterm. Give short loops and ask what is printed; let the student write the table of values before answering, and only then run the code.

name: Trace and write nested loops
description: predict the output of a loop inside a loop, also when the inner range depends on the outer loop variable, and write nested loops that run over all pairs or over a table.

name: Decide whether a while loop terminates
description: judge whether the condition of a while loop eventually becomes false, find how many passes it makes, and rewrite a for loop as an equivalent while loop.

name: Implement a mathematical sum with a loop
description: turn sum notation into a loop with an accumulator, with the first and the last index right, and compute terms with powers, factorials and alternating signs correctly.

name: Search and sort a list with loops
description: find the largest or the smallest element, count or collect the elements that match a condition, find the positions of a value, and recognise what a simple sorting algorithm such as bubble sort does.

name: List
description:
List: an ordered collection of elements of any type, other lists included, that can be changed after it is made.
Index: the position of an element, counted from 0; a negative index counts from the end, so a[-1] is the last element.

name: Index and slice lists
description: pick out elements and sublists with indices, negative indices and slices a[i:j:s] (where j is not included), including nested indexing such as a[1][0] and indices that are themselves taken from a list.
instruction: Exam questions often chain lookups, as in y[x[0]+1]. Work from the innermost bracket outwards.

name: Build and change lists
description: build lists with append, +, * and list(range(...)), find the length with len, test membership with in, find a position with index, and predict the length and the content of the result.

name: Build lists with list comprehensions
description: write and read list comprehensions, with and without an if-filter, and rewrite one as an ordinary for loop with append.

name: Loop over several lists at once
description: loop over two or more lists in step with zip, over index and element together with enumerate, or over the indices with range(len(...)), and choose the one that suits the task.

name: Store a table in nested lists
description: build a table as a list of rows or of columns, loop over it with nested loops, and pick out a row, a column or a single entry.

name: Tuple and unpacking
description:
Tuple: an ordered sequence like a list, written with parentheses, that cannot be changed after it is made. A function that returns several values returns a tuple.
Unpacking: assigning the elements of a tuple or list to several names at once, as in x, y = point or a, b = b, a.

name: Mutable objects and references
description:
Mutable object: an object that can be changed in place, like a list or a dictionary; numbers, strings and tuples are immutable.
Reference: b = a makes b a second name for the same object, so a change to the list through b is also seen through a; a.copy() makes a new list.

name: Dictionary
description:
Dictionary: a collection of key-value pairs where each value is looked up by its key, not by a position.
Key: an immutable value, often a string or a number, that occurs only once in the dictionary.

name: Build and use dictionaries
description: create a dictionary, add, change and delete entries, test whether a key is present, loop over keys and values with items, and use a dictionary of dictionaries as a register.

name: Function, argument and return value
description:
Function: a named block of code that runs when it is called.
Argument: a value passed to the function in the call; inside the function it is known by the parameter's name.
Return value: the value the function sends back with return. A function without return gives None, and printing a value inside a function is not the same as returning it.

name: Write a function from a formula
description: implement a mathematical formula as a Python function with suitable parameters and a return statement, and call it with given values.

name: Call functions with positional, keyword and default arguments
description: define parameters with default values (placed after those without), call a function with positional and keyword arguments, and decide whether a given call is legal and what it returns.

name: Local and global variables
description:
Local variable: a variable created inside a function, which exists only while the function runs and hides a global variable of the same name.
Global variable: a variable defined in the main program, which a function can read but does not change by assigning to the same name.

name: Trace code with function calls
description: predict the output of a program that defines and calls functions, including calls inside calls, functions that return several values, and names that exist both inside and outside a function.

name: Pass a function as an argument
description: pass a function, by its name or written as a lambda, to another function such as a root finder or a numerical derivative, and tell a correct call such as solve(lambda x: x**2 - 2, 1) from one that passes an expression instead of a function.
instruction: Explain lambda here if the student has not met it: lambda x: x**2 is a function written on one line, the same as def f(x): return x**2.

name: Implement a piecewise-defined function
description: implement a function given by different formulas on different intervals with if-elif-else, with no gaps or overlaps at the ends of the intervals and no more tests than needed.

name: Syntax error, runtime error and logic error
description:
Syntax error: code that breaks Python's grammar, so that nothing runs.
Runtime error: the program starts, but stops with an error message at a line that cannot be carried out.
Logic error: the program runs to the end but gives the wrong answer.

name: Common error messages
description:
NameError: a name is used before it has been defined
TypeError: an operation on a value of the wrong type, such as '3' + 4
ValueError: a value of the right type that cannot be used, such as float('abc')
IndexError: an index outside the list or array
KeyError: a key that is not in the dictionary
ZeroDivisionError: division by zero
SyntaxError: code that breaks Python's grammar
IndentationError: a line indented wrongly
AssertionError: an assert whose test is False

name: Find the line where a program fails
description: read code or an error message, find the first line that raises an error and which error it is, including an index one past the end of a list or array and a name used outside the function it was defined in.

name: Test function
description:
Test function: a function whose name starts with test_, that takes no arguments, computes a result with the function being tested and compares it with a known expected value; it prints nothing when the test passes.
assert: a statement that raises an AssertionError, with an optional message, if its condition is False.

name: Write a test function
description: write a test function for a given function with expected values worked out by hand, compare floats with a tolerance, as in abs(expected - computed) < tol, rather than with ==, and choose test cases that cover every branch.

name: Find and fix a logic error
description: find why a program gives the wrong answer by printing intermediate values or comparing with a hand calculation, fix it, and check a suggested fix, from a fellow student or an AI assistant, by running it on a case with a known answer.

name: Read input from the user and the command line
description: read values with input() and sys.argv, convert them from strings to numbers with int or float, and say what sys.argv holds for a given terminal command.

name: Read data from a text file
description: open a file with with open(...), skip header lines, split each line into words, convert the numbers, and collect the values in lists.

name: Write results to a text file
description: open a file for writing and write formatted lines to it, one line per entry, with a header.

name: Exception and try-except
description:
Exception: what Python raises when a line cannot be carried out; if nothing catches it, the program stops with an error message.
try-except: runs the code in try, and if an exception of a named type is raised there, jumps to the matching except instead of stopping.
raise: a statement that raises an exception on purpose.

name: Handle errors with try-except
description: catch specific exceptions such as IndexError and ValueError to give the user a helpful message, raise an exception for invalid input, and predict which except branch runs for given input.

name: Read a file into a dictionary
description: read a file of records into a dictionary, or a dictionary of dictionaries, keyed by one of the columns, join names that contain spaces back together, update the entries, and write the result back to a file.

name: Array and vectorisation
description:
Array: a numpy object holding a fixed number of elements of one type, on which arithmetic works element by element.
Vectorisation: computing on whole arrays at once instead of element by element in a Python loop.

name: numpy functions to know by heart
description:
np.linspace(a, b, n): n evenly spaced numbers from a to b, both included
np.zeros(n): an array of n zeros
np.zeros_like(x): an array of zeros with the same shape as x
np.arange(a, b, d): the numbers from a up to but not including b, in steps of d
np.array(a): an array made from the list a
np.sum(x): the sum of the elements of x
np.exp, np.sin, np.cos, np.sqrt, np.log: the functions applied to every element of an array
np.pi: the number pi

name: Create and fill arrays
description: create arrays with linspace, zeros and zeros_like, fill them element by element in a loop, and work out the length and the spacing of a linspace from its arguments.

name: Evaluate a formula on a whole array
description: compute function values for a whole array without a loop, using numpy's functions rather than those in math, and explain why an ordinary if-test fails when its argument is an array.

name: Explain the difference between a list and an array
description: predict the result of +, * and ** on lists and on arrays (2*x repeats a list but doubles every element of an array), and say when each is the better choice.

name: Index two-dimensional arrays
description: create an array with np.zeros((m, n)), read and set elements with A[i, j], and pick out a whole row or column with A[i, :] and A[:, j].

name: Plot curves with matplotlib
description: plot one or more curves in the same figure with plt.plot, add axis labels, a title and a legend, and explain what a given plotting script will show.

name: Read data from a file and plot it
description: read columns of numbers from a file into arrays and plot them, with labelled axes and units.

name: Class and object
description:
Class: the definition of a new type, which bundles data with the functions that work on it.
Object: one value of that type, also called an instance, made by calling the class.

name: Attribute, method, constructor and self
description:
Attribute: a value stored in an object, written self.a inside the class.
Method: a function defined inside a class.
Constructor: the method __init__, which runs when an object is made and usually stores the arguments as attributes.
self: the first parameter of every method, which refers to the object the method is called on.

name: Write a class with a constructor and methods
description: write a class whose constructor stores parameters as attributes and whose methods use them, and create and use objects of the class.

name: Special methods
description:
Special method: a method whose name starts and ends with two underscores, which Python calls behind an ordinary operation.
__call__: runs when an object is called like a function, as in f(x).
__str__: returns the string that print shows for the object.
__add__, __sub__, __mul__: run for +, - and * between objects.

name: Trace code that uses classes
description: predict the output of code that creates objects, changes their attributes and calls their methods, special methods included.

name: Implement a function with parameters as a class
description: write a class whose constructor stores the parameters of a mathematical function and whose __call__ evaluates it, so that f = F(a, b) can be used as f(x), and add __str__ to print the formula.

name: Implement arithmetic for your own class
description: implement __add__, __sub__, __mul__ and __str__ for a class such as a vector or a polynomial, returning a new object of the same class, also when the two operands have different lengths.

name: Inheritance
description:
Subclass: a class defined from another class, the superclass, which inherits all its attributes and methods.
Overriding: defining a method in the subclass with the same name as one in the superclass, so that the subclass's version is used.
super(): calls the superclass's version of a method from inside the subclass.

name: Write a subclass
description: write a subclass that reuses the superclass's constructor and methods and overrides only what differs, and check with isinstance which class an object belongs to.

name: Series and partial sum
description:
Series: an infinite sum of terms.
Partial sum: the sum of the first N terms, used as an approximation to the series.
Taylor series: a series in powers of x that approximates a function, such as exp(x) as the sum of x^k/k! for k from 0.

name: Approximate a function with a series
description: implement a partial sum of a series as a function of x and N that works for both numbers and arrays, and tabulate or plot its error against the exact function as N grows.

name: Finite-difference approximation
description:
Finite difference: an approximation of a derivative from function values at nearby points, such as (f(x+h) - f(x))/h (forward) or (f(x+h) - f(x-h))/(2h) (central).
Step size: the distance h between the points; a smaller h gives a smaller error until round-off error takes over.

name: Approximate a derivative numerically
description: implement a finite-difference formula for a first or second derivative as a function of f, x and h, and show how the estimate changes as h is reduced.

name: Approximate an integral with the trapezoidal or midpoint rule
description: implement the trapezoidal or the midpoint rule for a function f on [a, b] with n subintervals, with a loop or vectorised, and call it with a function as argument.

name: Root and iterative root finding
description:
Root: a value x where f(x) = 0.
Iterative method: a method that improves a guess step by step until |f(x)|, or the change from the last step, is below a tolerance.
Bisection: halves an interval in which f changes sign.
Newton's method: replaces x by x - f(x)/f'(x).
Secant method: Newton's method with f'(x) replaced by the slope through the two latest points.

name: Find a root numerically
description: implement or use bisection, Newton's method or the secant method with a while loop, a tolerance and a maximum number of iterations, and call a given solver correctly with functions as arguments.

name: Turn a mathematical description into a program
description: read a mathematical description of a scientific problem, sketch the steps in plain words, and write a program that carries them out with suitable functions, loops and data structures.

name: Check a numerical method by refining it
description: test a numerical method by reducing the step size or increasing the number of terms or time steps, tabulate the error against a known answer, and judge when the result is accurate enough.

name: Difference equation
description:
Difference equation: a rule that gives each term of a sequence from the term or terms before it, as in x[n] = x[n-1] + r/100*x[n-1].
Initial condition: the given first term or terms, such as x[0], that start the sequence.

name: Solve a difference equation with a loop
description: store a sequence in a list or array, set the initial value, and compute each term from the one before with a for loop, without index errors at either end.

name: Solve a system of difference equations
description: solve two or more coupled difference equations together, such as a predator-prey model, so that every new value is computed from the old values, and return the sequences.

name: Exponential and logistic growth
description:
Exponential growth: growth in proportion to the current size, x[n] = (1 + r/100)*x[n-1].
Logistic growth: growth that slows down as the size approaches the carrying capacity R, through a factor (1 - x[n-1]/R).
Carrying capacity: the largest population the environment can sustain.

name: Model growth with a difference equation
description: set up and solve a model of exponential or logistic growth, interest or a loan from a description in words, and plot the result.

name: Ordinary differential equation
description:
Ordinary differential equation: an equation linking an unknown function u(t) to its derivative, written u' = f(t, u).
Initial value problem: an ODE together with a starting value u(0) = u0.
Right-hand side: the function f(t, u), which in a program is a Python function.

name: Forward Euler method
description:
Forward Euler: steps from t[n] to t[n+1] = t[n] + dt with u[n+1] = u[n] + dt*f(t[n], u[n]), which replaces the derivative by a forward difference.
Time step: dt = T/N when the interval [0, T] is divided into N steps.

name: Implement Forward Euler for a scalar ODE
description: write a function that takes f, u0, T and N, fills arrays of time points and solution values with Forward Euler, and returns both; and do the same for another explicit method given by its formulas.

name: System of ODEs
description:
System of ODEs: several coupled equations written in vector form u' = f(t, u), where u is an array of unknowns and f returns an array of the same length.
Solution array: a two-dimensional array u[n, i] holding component i at time step n.

name: Solve a system of ODEs with Forward Euler
description: write the right-hand side of an ODE system as a function that returns a list or array, and solve the system with Forward Euler in a two-dimensional solution array.

name: Implement backward Euler for a simple ODE
description: explain why the backward Euler update is an equation for u[n+1] rather than a formula, rearrange it by hand for a linear ODE such as u' = -a*u, and implement the resulting update.

name: The ODESolver class hierarchy
description:
ODESolver: a superclass that stores the right-hand side and the initial condition and steps through an array of time points, for one equation or a system.
Solver subclass: a class such as ForwardEuler or RungeKutta4 that only defines the method advance, which computes one step.

name: Solve an ODE with an ODESolver class
description: create a solver object from a given subclass, set the initial condition, call solve with an array of time points, and unpack and plot the solution.

name: Implement a new ODE solver as a subclass
description: implement a method given by its formulas, such as Heun's or a Runge-Kutta method, as a subclass of ODESolver that overrides only advance.

name: Model a scientific system with ODEs
description: write the right-hand side of a model such as SIR, predator-prey or planetary motion as a function or as a class with the parameters as attributes, solve it, plot the components, and interpret the curves.
